Had to pay for mustard !!
Apr 2026 • Friends
French Onion Soup good flavor but too sweet. Caesar salad was OK. Panfried Foie Gras was good but small. Duck Confit was very ordinary. We were asked to pay extra for mustard… WHAT ??
Written April 25, 2026
Arnaud J
Dear Guest,

Thank you for your feedback.

We’re pleased to read that you overall found the onion soup, foie gras and Caesar salad enjoyable, even if not fully to your taste.

Regarding the foie gras, it is served as an individual starter portion (approximately 60g), designed for one guest. When shared between four people, it may naturally feel a bit limited.

As for our cuisine, we are a casual French bistro and aim to offer traditional, straightforward dishes, such as our duck confit, prepared in a classic and authentic style. Nothing overly elaborate, our guests usually visit us for honest, quality, and traditional (ordinary) French food.

Regarding our complimentary and extra items policy: we offer one complimentary serving of homemade bread and butter to start the meal. Additional bread may be offered during the meal for certain dishes such as cheese or cold cut platters. For other requests, additional bread and butter are charged.

We also do not serve complimentary water, as tap water in Vietnam is not drinkable. Certain items such as imported Dijon mustard are also charged, as they are premium products. On the other hand, we are happy to provide condiments such as ketchup and mayonnaise complimentary, as they are locally sourced.

We understand that these practices may not align with every guest’s expectations, but they are applied consistently and allow us to maintain the quality and balance of our offering.

We appreciate you sharing your perspective and will continue working to improve. We hope to have the opportunity to welcome you again in the future.

Merci et a bientôt.

Written September 30, 2025
Arnaud J
Bonjour Didier,

Merci pour votre retour. Nous sommes content de voir que vous avez apprécié votre plat. 

Concernant le pain, nous servons 1 petit pain avec beurre à tous les clients une fois la commande passée. Nous servons le pain à volonté uniquement pour certains plats comme les planches de charcuteries ou de fromages par exemple. Pour les autres plats nous informons les clients qu'il y a un supplément pour le pain additionnel (VND 10.000/pièce ou 0.30 euros). Nous avons vérifié avec la serveuse qui nous a confirmé vous avoir informé mais il y a surement eu une incompréhension dans la communication, veuillez nous en excuser. Les pains sont entièrement fait maison tous les matins. 

Les prix sont indiqués en Vietnam Dongs et n'incluent pas les taxes gouvernementales (VAT) qui sont de 10%. L'information est inscrite sur les menus en bas de page. 

Pour finir, les menus sont en effets uniquement traduits en Vietnamiens et en Anglais mais nous sommes justement en train de les traduire en Français, en Japonais, en Coréen et en Chinois pour le confort de notre clientèle internationale. 

Nous sommes désolé de ne pas avoir pu vous satisfaire pleinement et nous espérons pouvoir vous accueillir de nouveau prochainement pour mieux vous servir. 

Merci. A bientot.

Worst French Food in 15 Years
Sep 2025 • Couples
I’ve been living outside of France for 15 years, and this has been the worst French food I have eaten during that time. I would rate all three dishes a 0. We had escargots, which were cooked outside their shells and tasteless. The foie gras was also tasteless, with a hint of bitterness. The duck Parmentier was flavorless and even had a sharp bone inside. 

The service was subpar; when the server first asked how things were going, I replied, “not great,” and then there was silence. Later, when they asked for a second time, I pointed out the bones in the Parmentier, and they just took the dish to show the kitchen without any further response. 

We were served bread that was so hot we had to wait five minutes to eat it, and unfortunately, it was also tasteless. The wine prices were the most expensive I’ve seen in Asia, and the bill was excessively high with a 10% service surcharge. There was no discount for the bones, and no apologies were offered for the poor experience. This was the most expensive meal I’ve had in a while, and it was also the worst experience I’ve encountered in two decades. At this level of mediocrity, this is very close to being a tourist trap and would probably close doors in France.
Read more
Written September 13, 2025
Arnaud J
Dear Stéphanou,

Thank you for taking the time to share online your feedback about your last visit in our restaurant. We always value guest comments as long as they are honest and even if your review is the worst we had in the last 2 decades spent working in the Hospitality, Food & Beverage industry.

First of all, we would like to apologize for not being able to meet any of your expectations last night in terms of food or service.

Regarding the food. You are right, we import unshelled Burgundy snails, cook them with butter, garlic and parsley, then display them in shells. This is a common way of cooking French snails that most restaurants in Vietnam apply as we can only import unshelled snails here. This dish is known to be very strong in flavors, salty and garlicky. We are sorry to read that you personally describe it as tasteless.

Our Foie Gras terrine is made with imported whole duck liver from South-West of France. We cook it following traditional recipes.

Both the Foie Gras and Burgundy snails are among the most popular dishes in our restaurant for many years. After being informed by the waitress that you did not like those starters, our chef has checked again quality and seasoning and confirmed they were good according to our standards so we are sorry to read that it did not match your personal taste.

About the Duck Parmentier. It is known to be very strong in flavors, a bit peppery and spicy. We are sorry to read that you personally describe it as tasteless.

About the small piece of bone you found inside, it comes from the duck leg. This should not happen and this is our bad. Our waitress has apologized about it.

Talking about the bread. We make it ourself and finish baking it “a la minute” upon guest arrivals. It is famous for being hot, crusty outside with soft white crumb inside. Maybe yours was served a bit too hot. We are sorry to read that you had to wait 5 minutes to let the bread cool down.

Regarding the wine. You ordered a glass of red wine from South-West of France at VND 195.000 which is the second most affordable wine on our list. Vietnam applies a total of +/- 200% taxes on imported wine. We are confident our prices are reasonable compare to the domestic market. It is not easy to find a decent French wine under VND 200.000/glass in similar restaurants.

Finally regarding the billing, as written on our menus, prices does not includes 10% of VAT for government taxes. We are sorry to read that you felt our restaurant was too pricey. We are a casual/classy dining restaurant. There are many more expensive or more affordable options in town.

Regarding the service, our waitress has talked with you for few minutes at the end of the meal to understand what was wrong so we could improve ourselves in the future. She tried her best to understand and satisfy you but it seems that nothing we could possibly do, would have been enough to satisfy you last night.

Because you have eaten entirely the 3 dishes that you exaggeratedly and personally would rate “0”, we did not offered a discount but we did offered free dessert, tea or coffee and you declined.

We are truly sorry to bring such a bad experience for you last night but we also feel your comments are not reflecting the reality of our daily work.

We serve around 15.000 guests a year since 2020, 40% are local residents and 60% are travelers. We are letting them judging if we are a tourist trap or not.

Furthermore we cannot talk about the market in France but here in Vietnam, sadly we have seen many restaurants closing their doors since our opening in 2017. 9 years later we are still here, open 6 days a week trying humbly our best to offer not Michelin dining level but authentic, affordable and quality French dining experience.

Merci et a bientôt.
